policy_title: Stop supermarket price fixing and support direct sales for farmers
stated: Reform UK will grant powers to the Competitions and Markets Authority to ensure fair pricing and stop supermarket price fixing. They will also help farmers sell produce directly to the public and change planning laws to support farm shops with zero business rates.

source.quote: Stop Supermarket Price Fixing Grant powers to the Competitions and Markets Authority to ensure fair pricing. Help farmers sell their produce directly to the public. Change planning laws to support farm shops with zero business rates.

bearing_set.reason: Anti-price-fixing powers targeting supermarkets directly target food prices, a core component of the cost-of-living basket; if effective, consumer food costs could fall materially.

Fair-pricing rules and direct-sales support (including zero business rates for farm shops) directly affect farmers' income, business viability, and security of livelihood — a non-negligible effect on good work and fair pay for that sector.

Zero business rates for farm shops and planning-law changes to enable direct sales reduce operating costs and regulatory barriers for small agricultural businesses, bearing on business formation, rural economic dynamism, and producer living standards — all O13 indicators.

membership_note: Two genuine bearings: the anti-price-fixing strand bears on consumer food costs (O2); the direct-sales/farm-shop strand bears on agricultural business viability and rural prosperity (O13). Fiscal cost of business-rates relief is likely negligible at macro scale (farm shops are a niche sector) and does not clear the O12 non-negligible bar. O4 was considered for farmer incomes but farmers are predominantly self-employed owner-operators, making this more an O13 (aggregate opportunity/business dynamism) effect than a distributional labour-market one.
